States: `enforced` = a mechanism and passing tests cover the whole statement; `partial` = a named mechanism covers part of the statement, or all of it without tests; the gap names the rest; `absent` = no mechanism in this repository.

| C-01 | crypto | LEMMA | partial | Encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. | server.put() seals each value with seal(), which is AESGCM with a 256-bit key from new_key(), before storing it | `vaultlite/crypto.py#AESGCM.generate_key(bit_length=256)`<br>`vaultlite/server.py#STORE[name] = seal(MASTER_KEY`<br>`tests/test_crypto.py` | There is no storage at rest: STORE is an in-process dict, nothing is written to disk, so 'at rest' has no persistence layer to protect. Secret names are kept in clear as dict keys. MASTER_KEY defaults to None and no code reads VAULTLITE_KEY, so the server cannot run outside tests. No test asserts that STORE holds ciphertext rather than plaintext. |
| C-02 | crypto | LEMMA | enforced | Every secret has its own random nonce. | seal() draws a fresh 12-byte nonce from os.urandom for every call and prepends it to the ciphertext | `vaultlite/crypto.py#nonce = os.urandom(12)`<br>`tests/test_crypto.py` | — |
| C-03 | server | LEMMA | absent | Zero-knowledge server: the server never sees plaintext secrets. | — | — | The code does the opposite: server.py holds MASTER_KEY (its own docstring says so), seal() receives the plaintext value in put(), and get() decrypts and returns plaintext. Zero knowledge would need client-side encryption with keys the server never holds; none exists. |
